title: Scheduled alerts: never miss a move
summary: Ask Astor to check your stocks every morning, weekly, before a company reports or when a condition is met, and get a text with what it found.
body_markdown:
## How do earnings alerts work for stocks you own?


US public companies file a quarterly report with the SEC for each of the first three quarters of their fiscal year, plus an annual report after the fourth. So if you own 15 stocks (an illustrative number), that’s roughly 60 reports a year.


Astor already follows the earnings dates of every position you own. On top of that, you can ask for a check before a company reports, so you know what to watch for going in. Astor can also schedule its own follow-up after a company you own reports, so you hear what changed without having to ask.


Here’s a hypothetical. Say you own a software company that reports after the close on Thursday. You could ask Astor for a note that morning on what to watch for. After the results are out, Astor can set itself a check-in and text you what changed and whether it matters for your position.
